newsitem.title: USA: USWC crudes up with NYMEX, Canadian crude watched.
newsitem.headline: USWC crudes up with NYMEX, Canadian crude watched.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices rose Monday with energy futures, while traders waited to see if Canadian crude would be diverted West following the shutdown of major pipelines into the Midwestern states.
IPL on Monday said a power outage in Minnesota shut three pump station's along its Interprovincial pipeline system and stopped one million barrels per day (bpd) of crude flow.
IPL could deliver backed-up crude to Washington state, via the 172,000 bpd Trans Mountain Pipe Line, traders said.
"If it's not back up today, it could push Canadian into the Northwest," one California trader said.
Canadian imports, which compete with ANS, could push the ANSmarket lower, at a time of increasing South American volumes.

Discounts for local benchmark crude Alaska North Slope (ANS) were flat Monday at $1.05 under West Texas Intermediate, following a deal late last that increased the discount three cents from late March.
BP lowered its offer Monday to $0.95 under WTI.
The outright price for ANS rose 38 cents from Friday to $18.38/18.58 a barrel.
California heavy and light grades remained flat early Monday.
